analysis.title: Shell Plc (SHEL.AS): 3Q26 First Take: Strong results with 19% OCF beat drive buyback upgrade to $5bn in Q3
key_insights: Shell 3Q26 post-tax operating profit was US$11,534 mn, 4% above company-compiled consensus of US$11,068 mn. Adjusted CCS earnings were US$10,814 mn, 5% above consensus of US$10,329 mn.

The beat reflected high refining margins, high realised LNG prices and high Integrated Gas volumes. Lower crude and oil products trading and optimisation, higher well write-offs and lower realised liquids prices partly offset it.
Cash flow from operations before working capital was US$21.7 bn, 19% above consensus of US$18.2 bn. GS attributes it mainly to Adjusted EBITDA and net cash inflows from derivatives of $3.4 bn.
Capex of US$7.9 bn left FCF (pre-OWC) of US$13.8 bn for the quarter.
Net debt fell US$10.8 bn quarter on quarter to US$39.7 bn from US$41.7 bn at the end of 2Q26 as stated in the report. Gearing fell to 20% from 23% at 2Q26, versus the GS estimate of 21%.

Shell completed the aggregate US$4.2 bn of buybacks announced at 2Q26 and announced a new US$5.0 bn buyback programme, up from the US$3.0 bn previously expected, to be completed by the 4Q26 results announcement.
FY2026 cash capex guidance was cut to US$23-25 bn including ARC from US$24-26 bn, versus FY2025 actual of US$21 bn.

4Q26 guidance: Integrated Gas production of about 1,080-1,180 kboe/d reflecting the ARC Resources acquisition, LNG liquefaction of 7.3-7.9 mn tonnes, and Upstream production of 1,700-1,900 kboe/d including weather allowance in the Gulf of America.

4Q26 guidance also includes Marketing sales volumes of 2,400-2,600 kb/d, refinery utilisation of 92-100%, Chemicals plant utilisation of 78-86%, and a Corporate Adjusted Earnings net expense of about $600-800 mn.

Segment post-tax operating profit versus consensus: E&P US$3,485 mn (+3%), Integrated Gas US$3,037 mn (+4%), Marketing US$1,164 mn (+1%), Chemicals & Products US$3,855 mn (+3%), Renewables & Energy Solutions US$289 mn versus US$148 mn.
GS rates Shell Buy with a 12-month price target of €53.0 for SHEL.AS and US$123.0 for SHEL, based on 5.5x EV/DACF applied to 2026E cash flow.

market_movers.rationale: 3Q26 post-tax operating profit was 4% above consensus and cash flow 19% above, with the buyback raised to US$5.0 bn. The target uses 5.5x EV/DACF on 2026E cash flow, and GS sees 16.9% upside from $105.19.

earnings_insights: Shell 3Q26 reported 10/29: post-tax operating profit US$11,534 mn versus company-compiled consensus US$11,068 mn (+4%). GS estimate was US$11,900 mn.
Adjusted CCS earnings reported 3Q26: US$10,814 mn versus company-compiled consensus US$10,329 mn (+5%). GS estimate was US$11,200 mn.
CFO ex-working capital reported 3Q26: US$21,682 mn versus consensus US$18,178 mn (+19%) and GS estimate US$17,000 mn.
Capex reported 3Q26: US$7,922 mn versus GS estimate US$5,800 mn.
Chemicals and products post-tax operating profit reported US$3,855 mn versus consensus US$3,743 mn, but below the GS estimate of US$5,000 mn.
Reported production 3Q26: 2,574 kboepd total versus GS estimate 2,550, with oil at 1,460 and gas at 1,114 kboepd.
GS estimates FY2026E P/E of 8.0x, EV/DACF 4.7x, dividend yield 3.0% and FCF yield 13.3%.
risk_factors: Lower oil prices and refining margins.
Negative surprises to growth or capex.
